messages:
marcus: seeing a flurry of Pending GPUs in us-west1-a since 07:12. CA keeps logging "no capacity in zone" even though quota/rate look fine. Pods stuck with nodeSelector: nvidia-t4, toleration to gpu-pool.
alyssa: yup saw it, trying to repro. kube-scheduler reports "no nodes available for pods with GPUs" and CA is saying "no nodegroup available to increase" :thinking:
sanjay: what's the autoscaler config? if the nodepool is created with max=0 or autoscaling disabled CA won't grow it. also cross-cluster failover needs taints/labels consistent across clusters.
marcus: autoscaler flags look normal, here's the pod event snippet:
```
Events:
  Type    Reason            Age   From               Message
  ----    ------            ----  ----               -------
  Warning FailedScheduling  2m    default-scheduler  0/20 nodes are available: 20 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu.
```
alyssa: CA logs:
```
E0318 07:13:01 cluster_autoscaler.go:123] no node groups to expand
```
alyssa: CA is attached to the wrong ASG/node-pool tag set for that cluster. Looks like last week's rename broke discovery when we added regional nodepools.
sanjay: ah — we moved to regional node-pools (us-west1) but labels still expected zone-scoped names. CA auto-discovery relies on label: k8s.io/cluster-autoscaler/enabled=true and node group name pattern. If mismatch, it won't scale.
tess: if we enable cross-cluster failover, we also need to ensure workload can tolerate node labels & storage access. Models are ~30GB weights, copying at scale will hit network and egress costs. :money_with_wings:
marcus: proposal: 1) fix CA discovery labels on west cluster 2) add a warm standby regional pool in us-west2 with pre-pulled model cache 3) implement a lightweight redirect controller to prefer local zone but failover to standby cluster via k8s endpoint mirroring
sanjay: agree but two warnings: a) network path between clusters currently goes over VPC peering with 30-80ms p95, adds tokenization latency for chat workloads; b) egress costs: pulling weights across regions -> multiply by concurrent replicas.
ops-bot: FYI incident-972 has a note: "us-west1 GPU quota hitting burst limit at 07:00" — flagged for follow-up.
alyssa: alternative: redis-backed artifact cache in each region so standby only fetches once, and we use rsync/cron to pre-warm between low-usage windows. That reduces live-copy pressure.
tess: also consider using mixed node-pools: keep a small on-demand pool for immediate burst (min=1) and scale-out preemptible for bulk. CA needs scaleUpDelay=0 but careful with scaleDownUnneededTime to avoid thrashing.
marcus: action items: @sanjay update CA discovery labels and restart CA by EOD, @alyssa prototype cross-cluster redirect controller + cache pre-warm plan, @tess cost estimate for inter-region pulls and on-demand standby. I'll coordinate with infra on IAM for artifact-sync.
deploy-bot: schedule: rolling restart of cluster-autoscaler on infra-west scheduled for 2026-03-18T18:30Z by marcus (ETA 10m) :white_check_mark:
sanjay: preflight checklist before restart: snapshot autoscaler config, run `kubectl get cm -n kube-system cluster-autoscaler-config -o yaml`, confirm node-pools have label `cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/enabled=true`, and ensure cloud API quotas for gpus are not at soft limit.
alyssa: I'll also add a short e2e: create a job that requests a tiny GPU pod with nodeSelector and verify CA expands the regional pool within 90s. Posting results here after test. :shipit:
